Publisher: Unknown—pre-1900 Bengali script.
Country of publication: India || Oṃ, salutation to the Supreme Goddess.
In the Kāmākhyā Tantra, the first chapter;
the venerable Goddess said:
O Blessed One, knower of all phenomena, lover of all sciences, Lord; you whose heart is always blissful, illuminator of all scriptures! || 1 ||
All the tantras and numerous Yāmalas have been heard;
O God, by your grace, all those sciences have borne their fruit.
O Lord, tell me: do you know this Tantra, which is the essence of essences?
This place is exceedingly secret; therefore, I am intent on hearing it.
The illustrious Śiva said:
Listen with joy, O auspicious goddess, my beloved as dear as life;
Kāmākhyā, the bestower of boons, is the Great Knowledge (Mahāvidyā) in the form of the Yoni.
She is the giver of boons, the giver of bliss, eternal, and the increaser of great prosperity;
she is considered the mother of all and the savior of all. || 5 ||
And she is the delight of all, both gross and subtle, ever auspicious;
I shall proclaim her Tantra—listen with careful attention.
Whichever practitioners achieve success in any of the various sciences,
Kāmākhyā bestows the fruit [of their efforts] wherever they may be and by whatever means.
Those people who are averse to Kāmākhyā are censured throughout the three worlds;
for without her, whose very essence is desire, there is no one else who bestows the wealth of spiritual accomplishments.
Kāmākhyā is always Dharma, and Kāmākhyā is indeed Artha;
Kāmākhyā is the attainment of desire, and Kāmākhyā is indeed Mokṣa.
O Goddess of gods, that alone is Nirvāṇa; that alone is declared to be Sāyujya; it is Sālokya and Saharūpa; Kāmākhyā is the supreme goal.
O Goddess, you are the state of Śiva, the state of Brahmā, the state of Viṣṇu, and even the state of the Moon;
you are the divinity of all the gods, certainly able to assume any form at will.
Indeed, the nature of all sciences as well as all worldly speech is entirely the very form of the Great Goddess known as Kāmā.
Look, look, my beloved! Having reflected upon everything within your own heart, you will see that nothing exists in the three worlds apart from Kāmākhyā. (13)
O Goddess, the Great Vidyās numbering one hundred million have been proclaimed in the Tantras and other scriptures; yet among them all, the Ṣoḍaśī is considered the very essence of essences.
And the cause of that, O Goddess, is Kāmākhyā, the Mother of the World;
just as, O Goddess, moonlight is born and again dissolves. (15)
Whatever things exist here, whether stationary or moving, eternal or transient—
truly, truly, and again truly— it is not born at all without her.
Thus ends the first chapter in the Śrī Kāmākhyā Tantra, in the dialogue between the Goddess and the Lord. 1.
Now begins the second chapter.
The venerable Śiva said:
"O Goddess, listen to the extraction of the mantra (mantroddhāra), which is higher than the highest."
Having known which, one shall accomplish a perfection that is difficult even for the gods to attain. || 1 ||
By the power of this mantra, one may delude the entire world;
O Goddess, one may delude even Brahmā and the other gods, just as a mother [deludes] her child. || 2 ||
O Goddess of the Suras, she can delude the gods, dānavas, gandharvas, kinnaras, and others in a mere instant, just as a king does among his subjects.
O Goddess, before the mantra are the king, his ministers and others, and all other human beings, as well as animals such as rams and the like. (4)
In an instant, celestial courtesans such as Urvaśī and others deluded the king’s city, including its elephants, horses, chariots, and so forth, as well as the king’s wives and attendants.
O Goddess, [the rites of] immobilization, killing, agitation, yawning, as well as melting, terrifying, causing hatred, and expulsion; || 6 ||
O Maheśvarī, the attraction of women, especially [this],
as well as subjugation and other [rites], the best of practitioners should accomplish.
Fire, wind, and the sun, which is a mass of water—by a mere sidelong glance, all these are held in check by the practitioner; it is not otherwise.
O beloved of my life, just as the victorious Kāmadeva, the knower of mantras, conquers the world,
there is nothing in the three worlds that is unattainable for him.
O Goddess, [the mantra] ending with *jṛmbhaṇa*, with the noose (*pāśa*) removed, together with the rider of the elephant of the expedition (*yātrāvāraṇarohaka*),
endowed with the deficient syllables, and furthermore joined with the *nāda* and *bindu*.
Having multiplied this [mantra] threefold, one should recite the mantra of the Kalpavṛkṣa;
the wise person should recite it once, twice, or even four times. (11)
Practitioners must perform the *sādhana* of Kāmākhyā among all the vidyās;
otherwise, there will be a loss of accomplishment and obstacles for them at every step.
Whether they be Śāktas, Vaiṣṇavas, Śaivas, or Gāṇapatyas—
all those observing the vow of Mahāmāyā were like bulls in an oil-press.
And its means of accomplishment, O Goddess, O beautiful one, belongs only to the Śāktas;
herein there is no purification of the wheels (cakras), nor any purification of time and so forth.
If this is performed, one goes to hell and everything belonging to him perishes;
O Goddess, this supreme practice is free from affliction and provides swift nourishment. 15.
The Goddess Śrī said: "O Lord of Gods, what is the destiny of one who entertains doubt regarding the bestowal of the mantras of Kālī and Tārā? Is there any deliverance for him, or not? (16)
Śrī Śiva said:
O Maheśvarī, we, Agni, and even Kāla—whatever beings have passed away, O Goddess of the gods—what can we say regarding the mantra of Kālikātāriṇī? (17)
O Dear One, if the counting of the wheels and other parts is performed out of ignorance or delusion regarding Kālī, Tārā, or Manu, one shall become a worm in the excrement of a dog.
And at the end of the aeon, O Great Goddess, there is no deliverance from it;
I shall now describe its worship, which bestows the accomplishment of the three worlds. (19)
O Goddess of gods, whatever accomplishment arises through *haṭha* and *haṭhayoga*, it is attained at that very moment; no deliberation should be made in this matter. (20)
Having prepared a circle of vermilion, the best of practitioners should draw a triangle within it and place his own seed-syllables in its center.
O Goddess, O Beloved, one should then draw a square and an eightfold vajra;
having performed the network of ritual placements (nyāsa), one should worship her in the eight directions.
The sage is declared to be Akṣobhya, the metre is said to be Anuṣṭubh, and the deity is Kāmākhyā, who is employed for the attainment of all perfections. (23)
One should perform the ritual placement (nyāsa) on the hands and limbs using one's own seed-syllable;
then, one should meditate upon Kāmākhyā, the bestower of desired fruits, who possesses the six long vowels.
Clad in red garments, intent on her supreme vow, adorned with a mark of vermilion,
she was stainless, her face radiant like the moon and her teeth gleaming white.
She was the supreme goddess, adorned with ornaments of gold, gems, and rubies,
and seated upon a lion-throne fashioned from various jewels and precious stones.
With a smiling face and the unsurpassed luster of a ruby,
she was dark-complexioned with full, high breasts, her eyes reaching to the roots of her ears.
With her side-long glances, she is the Supreme Goddess who bestows great prosperity;
she is irreproachable in every limb and surrounded by various branches of knowledge.
It was adorned by ḍākinīs, yoginīs, and vidyādharīs;
it was joined with beautiful women and made fragrant with various perfumes and other scents. || 29 ||
She was graced by female attendants holding betel leaves and other offerings in their hands,
and she awaited the prostrations of all the hosts of perfected beings (siddhas).
She has three eyes, she is the enchantress who wields the flower-bow and arrows,
and she listens even from the Kinnarīs to the discourse concerning the female and male organs.
She who is eager for discourse and counter-discourse with words as sweet as nectar, who is endowed with all virtues, and who is Śivā, an ocean of compassion. (32)
Then, O beloved of Hara, the practitioner, having meditated thus, should invoke the Goddess and worship her according to the prescribed rite.
With saffron and other such substances, with red flowers and fragrant blossoms, and especially with hibiscus, barley-alkali, vermilion, and oleanders.
O Goddess of the Gods, Kāmākhyā herself resides among the Karavīra flowers;
know that she likewise dwells among the Javā, Mālatī, and other such blossoms. (35)
The greatness of the karavīra cannot indeed be fully described;
however, by the offering of a javā flower, one attains the status of a Gaṇapati.
One should always worship the goddess Ambikā with the five principles (pañcatattva);
without the five principles, worship leads to malevolent magic (abhicāra).
Through the fivefold reality (pañcatattva), the grace of the Goddess arises in an instant;
by the fifth, O Great Goddess, the practitioner becomes Śiva. (38)
There is nothing equal to the five principles (pañcatattva) in the Kali age;
the five principles are the supreme Brahman, the five principles are the highest goal. || 39 ||
The five principles, O Great Goddess, are Sadāśiva;
the five principles are enjoyment and liberation—this is proclaimed as the Great Yoga. || 40 ||
O Goddess of the gods, by means of the five principles (pañcatattva), millions of great sins are destroyed in that very instant, just as fire consumes a heap of cotton.
Wherever the five principles (pañcatattva) are present, there the Goddess certainly dwells;
but where the five principles are lacking, the Mother of the World turns her face away.
Through liquor one rejoices in heaven; through meat, one becomes a lord of men;
through fish, one becomes the son of Bhairavī; and through the mudrā, one attains saintliness. 43.
Furthermore, O Great Queen, a man attains union with the Supreme;
when one worships the Goddess endowed with devotion, then everything is brought forth. || 44 ||
One should offer an *arghya* to the Goddess with white *svayambhū* flowers, auspicious substances produced from the *kuṇḍa* and *goḷa*, saffron and other ingredients, and liquor.

Having worshipped the Goddess with various offerings and oblations, including food and milk-rice (pāyasa), as well as garments, ornaments, and other articles, one should worship the surrounding deities (āvaraṇa).
O Śāṅkarī, one should worship Indra and the others there along with their respective yantras;
the best of practitioners should worship Kamalā and Vāṇī on the two sides.

O Goddess, she is the giver of food, the giver of wealth, the giver of happiness, and likewise the giver of victory; she is the giver of essence, the giver of delusion, and also the giver of prosperity and the giver of spiritual perfection.
She bestows prosperity and purity, as well as worldly enjoyment and liberation;
she grants emancipation and happiness, and likewise bestows knowledge and splendor.
O Śivā, these great goddesses, beginning with Ḍākinī, are always to be worshipped in the center of the yantra; likewise, the siddhis should be worshipped with effort. 50.
Then the practitioner should worship the six limbs of the Goddess and cast handfuls of flowers;
with a pure disposition, he should recite the mantra according to his capacity. (51)
Having offered the recitation (japa), one should satisfy the Supreme Deity with musical instruments and other offerings;
one should then recite hymns and armor-protective mantras (kavaca) and prostrate according to this rite. 52.
Then, having joined the Goddess Śeṣikā within his heart,
he should cast the remains of the offering (nirmālya) toward the northeast and fashion a triangle there.
The practitioner should receive the remains of the offering (nirmālya) together with the other practitioners out of a spirit of devotion;
he should then enjoy it according to the five principles (pañcatattva), following the prescribed rule and according to his own capacity. 54.
The means of accomplishment is rooted in Śakti; the recitation of mantras and so forth is rooted in Śakti;
even the recitations themselves are rooted in Śakti; and life itself is rooted in Śakti. || 55 ||
O Dear One, all austerity rooted in power yields results in this world, while that rooted in power yields results in the hereafter; likewise, the fourfold aim of life is rooted in power.
O Goddess, all things, both stationary and moving, are rooted in Śakti; without knowing this, sinners certainly go to Raurava.
Therefore, by all means and by the command of Śiva, practitioners should indeed drink the remains of the Śakti; otherwise, they go to the Raurava hell. 58.
O Goddess, whatever is given for the sake of Śakti becomes an offering made to the Devas;
all that action becomes fruitful—this is the truth, the absolute truth, O Mistress of the Kula. (59)
If one performs or causes the Kaula-cakra to be performed without a Śakti, he goes to a terrible hell, and there is no liberation for him. (50)
In this manner, O Dear One, whatever object the practitioner intends when worshipping the Goddess, having placed that very desire in his hand, he certainly triumphs. 61.
During the period of *puraścaraṇa*, the wise practitioner should recite the mantra one hundred thousand times;
he should then perform oblations with clarified butter, sugar, honey, and milk-rice in quantities equal to one-tenth of that number.
The lord of practitioners should satisfy [the deity] with waters mixed with sandalwood from the directions of the quarters,
and he should consecrate it with those kuśa grasses, perfumes, and other offerings.
O Goddess, one should feed the best of the twice-born with sweets equal to a tenth part of the initiation fee (abhiṣeka),
and the practitioners (sādhakas) who are devotees of the Goddess with the five types of offerings.
Having performed such worship, the practitioner becomes accomplished;
therefore, O Goddess, he will certainly become fit for the ritual applications.
All this, beginning with worship, brings pleasure to Kāmākhyā;
O Kuleśvarī, worship in the yonic wheel (yonicakra) produces great delight.
The worship of the source (yonipūjā) is the great worship; indeed, there is no other bestower of accomplishment equal to it.
Therein the wise one should worship the Goddess; she alone is the Goddess, and not otherwise.
O beloved, rites such as invocation and the like are not required there at all;
rather, one should smear it with perfumes and other substances and worship it with various offerings.
Great joy shall arise for the Goddess, and he becomes a Siddha at that very moment.
There is no worship equal to the worship of the Yoni within my own gnosis.
By kissing and licking [her] in the vulva, one surpasses the wish-fulfilling tree;
by the mere sight [of her], one becomes a sovereign of practitioners, and by touch, a deluder of all. (70)
The description of the union of the Linga and the Yoni increases the delight of Kāmākhyā;
that alone is her very life, O Girijā—what need is there for further words? (71)
Therefore, with every effort, one should perform the worship of the womb;
having approached the womb of another's wife, the wise man should worship it especially.
O Goddess, the womb of a courtesan is supreme; one should perform the practice there.
Success is attained in just three nights; no doubt should be entertained in this matter. (73)
One should joyfully accomplish [the rite] according to the rules in the midst of creepers during the appropriate season;
before long, one attains success that is difficult even for the gods to achieve. (74)
The practice of the *yonimudrā* is declared to be the most essential of all essentials;
O Goddess, without that practice, a great curse arises. (75)
O Goddess, that lowest of men who utters contempt or loathing for the womb shall, before long, go to the Raurava hell; O Goddess, this is the truth by the command of Śiva. (76)
O Goddess, one should dwell within the center of the womb; the Yoginīs reside in the hair.
Therefore, if one desires one's own welfare, one should not revile the womb. 77.
One who utters censure of the *yoni* perishes along with his lineage; but one who is intent on the praise of the *yoni*, O Goddess, becomes auspicious (*śiva*) at that very moment. 78.

What can we say regarding the greatness of the womb and the fruits of worshipping the womb? O you who can assume any form at will, please forgive whatever has been spoken [by me] out of fickleness. (79)
Thus ends the second chapter in the Śrī Kāmākhyā Tantra, in the dialogue between the Goddess and the Lord.
Now begins the third chapter.
O Pārvatī, listen with reverence as I proclaim the supreme mantra,
by the mere grace of which even Brahmā, Viṣṇu, and Śiva [attain their goals].
All the deities, beginning with Indra, become possessed of desire, O Goddess, as do the Gandharvas, Kinnaras, Vidyādharas, and others. || 2 ||
Having attained whose grace, the Yoginīs, Ḍākinīs, Vidyās, Bhairavīs, Nāyikās, and others, are endowed with their respective domains. || 3 ||
Having attained the mantra of Kāmākhyā, practitioners possess supreme fitness;
whatever adepts achieve success, whether in heaven, on earth, or in the netherworld, [it is through this]. || 4 ||
O Goddess, [one should utter] one's own three seed-syllables, followed by two wrathful syllables (krodha),
then the three seed-syllables of the Vadhū, and one should speak the name of Kāmā again.
One should arrange the word "prasīda" (be gracious) and the previous seed-syllables;
this mantra, ending with two *ṭha*s, is declared to be difficult to find in all tantras.
*Krīṃ krīṃ krīṃ huṃ huṃ strīṃ strīṃ, O Kāmākhyā, be gracious!
Krīṃ krīṃ krīṃ huṃ huṃ strīṃ strīṃ svāhā!* O Great Goddess, beginning with the *praṇava*, you are exceedingly difficult to attain within the three worlds.
She is the direct bestower of the four goals of human existence and the destroyer of great sins.
O Pārvatī, by the mere recollection of this mantra, all obstacles become agitated and perish like moths in a blazing fire.
Merely by receiving this mantra, a person becomes liberated while living;
enjoyment and liberation are in his hand, and he shall become beloved by all.
Lakṣmī herself covers [the house], and eloquent speech shall always dwell in his mouth;
sons, grandsons, and great-grandsons shall all be long-lived. || 10 ||
O Śaṅkarī, on this earth, at all sacred seats such as Kāmākhya and others, the script moves [manifests] for him alone; there is no need for deliberation in this matter.
Remembering his name, the members of the assembly bow down;
indeed, upon hearing his name even once, harmful beings flee.
Whatever accomplishments exist in heaven, on earth, or in the subterranean realm, they all attend upon the practitioners; of this there is no doubt. (13)
Upon seeing that lord of practitioners, the opponent falters at the mere sight of him;
all virtuous people in the assembly behold him as possessing the radiance of ten million suns. || 14 ||
O Maheśvarī, even with thousands of tongues and hundreds of millions of mouths, I am simply unable to fully describe this mantra.
O fair-faced one, all the rites such as the ritual placements (nyāsa) and worship have been previously described;
however, in the procedure for the preparatory rite (puraścaryā), one should recite the mantra six thousand times.
One should perform six hundred oblations and other rites according to the prescribed rule;
then the knower of mantras becomes perfected and capable in the practical applications. || 17 ||
Listen, O Great Goddess, to the meditation that bestows wealth, grain, and sons;
it destroys poverty, O Goddess, in an instant and not otherwise. (18)

She is exquisitely graceful in her attire, with a smiling face and three eyes, possessing a beauty that surpasses the splendor of the clouds; she is radiant in silk garments, enriched by the gestures of granting fearlessness and bestowing boons, and most magnificent with her jewel ornaments.
Seated upon a jeweled lion-throne on a pedestal at the foot of a celestial tree.
I bow to Bhavānī, who is unassailable by Hari, Hara, or Brahmā; whose very nature is the increase of wisdom;
who is an amorous woman anointed with the arrows of Madana; who bestows all desires; and whose form is the manifestation of the playful delight of all people.
I worship her who destroys the impurities of the Kali age and whose form is the source (yoni). || 20 ||
O Goddess, this meditation, which is more secret than the secret and destroys poverty, has been concealed in all tantras; it is now revealed because of your devotion. (21)
Having fashioned a tilaka with svayambhū flowers alone,
O Great Goddess, one should cause the Kula-śakti to enter into the brush.
With his mouth perfumed with camphor, the practitioner, being skillful, should joyfully kiss her;
O beloved, let his lower lip be like a bee agitated by a lotus.
And there he should cause a canopy of tooth-marks to be made;
intoxicated with passion, he should embrace her firmly, crushing her breasts.
The expert in sexual pleasure should delight her on the hips with nail-scratches, and he should repeatedly kiss her vulva, O Kuleśvarī. (25)
The hero should restrain his semen and insert his penis into the vagina;
O Dear One, he should satisfy her through strikes, by means of union and separation. (26)
Then, once the *liṅga* is established in the *yoni*, and having received her command,
one should recite the mantra one hundred and eight times with the desire to perform the fire-oblation (*homa*) and other rites.
For three days, the great sage, intent on meditation, should perform the recitation;
he shall obtain his mental object—of this there is no doubt. || 28 ||
O Goddess, having placed the creeper joined with the season upon the couch,
one should place a karavīra flower upon her liṅga.
Having seen that, O Goddess of the lords of gods, one should mutter [the mantra] eight thousand times for three days; then, O beloved, the devotion to the Goddess shall become unshakable.
He shall undoubtedly obtain wealth amounting to a hundred thousand;
it will constantly increase the bliss of that high-souled practitioner. (31)
Having kissed and worshipped the one hundred and eight birth-cavities (*yoni*), the virtuous person,
once again with the *liṅga* placed within the *yoni*, should perform the recitation (*japa*) eight thousand times.
O Maheśānī, one who is free from doubt shall always obtain wealth fivefold and remain ever happy; he shall constantly have union with a woman of noble character.
Having brought forth the creeper-like courtesan and having established the circle of the lineage (kulacakra),
the practitioner, with a joyful heart, should worship the Goddess within her womb.
One should recite the description of the *bhaga* and the *liṅga* in a melodious voice;
having gazed upon the *yoni*, one should mutter the mantra for seven nights without weariness. (35)

By performing this three hundred times every day, even he becomes a lord of supernatural powers (siddhīśvara) in the Kali age; O Goddess, there is no doubt that Dhanada (the Giver of Wealth) obeys his command.
If one performs the practice of the Yoni after having remembered the true Guru, then one attains perfection; otherwise, it is indeed merely a cause for laughter.
Thus ends the third chapter in the Śrī Kāmākhyātantra, in the dialogue between the Goddess and the Lord.
Now begins the fourth chapter.
The Śrī Devī said:
"O Mahādeva, O Lord, please explain the reality of the Guru in detail."
But how could such a weightiness, so difficult to bear, possibly arise in a human being? (1)
In that very matter, O Lord, who is the true guru and who has fallen away? Tell me, O Mahādeva, dispel this great and intense doubt of mine.
Having heard these words of the Goddess, the Lord Śaṅkara spoke:
"Listen to this most essential knowledge, which is for the benefit of the virtuous. (3)
The Guru is declared to be Sadāśiva; he is called Ādinātha, the God endowed with a vast body, whose form is existence, consciousness, and bliss. || 4 ||
The eternal Supreme Brahman, the illustrious Dharma, the Lord of the three qualities—
by your grace, O Great Goddess, I am Śiva, ageless and immortal.
For this very reason, the Guru is not merely a human being, but rather a mental construction;
just as there is worship of trees and so forth for the sake of the initiation of practitioners.
Whatever meditation one performs upon the lotus of the guru’s head as the giver of the mantra,
that same meditation is prescribed for the disciple’s head and not otherwise.
Therefore, O Great Goddess, how could there be a human guru? O Goddess, the status of being a guru in a human is a mere mental construction, not a reality.
Salutation to that venerable Guru by whom that state was revealed— the state which is of the form of an unbroken circle and by which all that is moving and unmoving is pervaded.
O Goddess, that state which is well-established is the one revealed by the man [who has realized it];
for this very reason, O Goddess, the attribution of "guru-ship" to a man is indeed merely a conceptual construction.
But it is not the case that either the teacher himself is base or both are foolish;
rather, it is when there is the recognition: "This one is my teacher" and "This one is indeed my disciple. (11)
The observer of study itself is the human teacher;
truly, liberation does not arise from the mere presence of a human teacher. (12)
Just as food is given to an eater by means of a vessel made of gold or other materials, O Goddess, so too is everything offered to him. (13)
O Maheśvarī, if that vessel is deemed fit for contemplation, yet it is broken,
then one should discard that vessel and satisfy oneself with another vessel.
Therefore, even a disciple should abandon a human being who is greedy and wicked;
for one who is disliked by the world, Sadāśiva is always enraged.
Just as the property of a king is given to the king by his subjects through the provinces and so forth, in the very same way, the giving of a disciple is an act of offering to him. 16.
If predatory beings such as Maṇḍala and others are remembered to be present right here,
one should always give [the offering] through another door, having avoided them all.
In all worlds, service to the guru is the means for attaining true knowledge;
through knowledge one attains liberation; therefore, knowledge is higher than the highest. (18)
Therefore, O beloved, one should abandon that guru who is indeed incapable of bestowing knowledge,
just as one who desires food abandons one who has no food.
When the threefold knowledge shines forth, that Guru is indeed Śiva himself;
therefore, setting aside the ignorant, one should seek refuge with the wise.
From knowledge, O Pārvatī, dharma arises eternally; from knowledge indeed comes wealth;
from knowledge one attains desire; and from knowledge comes stainless liberation.
For knowledge is indeed the supreme reality; there is nothing more essential than knowledge.
One worships the Lord for the sake of knowledge, for knowledge is the fruit of austerity.
Just as a bee, greedy for honey, goes from flower to another flower, so too a disciple, greedy for knowledge, should go from one teacher to another teacher. (23)
There are many gurus who seize the wealth of their disciples;
O Goddess, a true guru who removes the suffering of his disciples is rare to find. (24)
Salutations to that illustrious Guru, by whom the eye was opened for one blinded by the darkness of ignorance, using the ointment-stick of knowledge. (25)
Thinking thus, the best of practitioners should always conceive of the teacher as supreme;
for disciples devoted to Śiva find certainty in the wise one alone. (26)
He who is peaceful, self-controlled, of noble birth, always pure in heart, and a worshiper of the five principles—he is proclaimed as a true guru. || 27 ||
"If it is argued that he is known as an accomplished one (siddha) by many, being a protector of disciples and a performer of wonders through divine power, O beloved, he is called a true guru. (28)
He who speaks words that are agreeable, virtuous, and captivating to the mind, and who delivers instructions and counsel with impartiality—he alone is a true spiritual teacher (sadguru). (29)
He who is always intent upon the awakening and welfare of his disciples, and who is capable of both restraint and grace, is proclaimed as a true guru by the wise. (30)
One whose vision is always fixed upon the ultimate truth is proclaimed as the ultimate truth itself;
he who possesses devotion at the lotus feet of the Guru is remembered as a true Guru. || 31 ||

Having seen such a perfection of qualities, O Goddess, a disciple should approach a guru; having abandoned even a worthy guru [if he lacks these], there is no deliberation regarding time in this matter. (32)
One who possesses only a circle of disciples, who is a consumer of much, who is physically impaired, and who is constantly scrutinized by people—such a person is considered a guru in name only. (33)
If, upon seeing a disciple endowed with devotion through body, mind, or speech,
one does not feel sympathetic joy, that object [of devotion] is merely a matter of desire.

One who, through reprehensible action alone, seizes the wealth and other possessions of a disciple, and who disregards the world that desires the welfare of his disciples—he is the lowest of men; one should avoid him.
Having taken up the Great Vidyā, he who bestows the conduct of a hero goes to a terrible hell; his disciple, too, certainly falls.
For one who remains in the state of a beast and speaks of the mantra of Kālikā Tāriṇī or of the conduct according to reality (tattvācāra), he does not return from hell. 37.
Therefore, O Dear One, practitioners should always avoid a teacher who is a *paśu*;
the initiation of a *paśu* is declared to be the lowest, as it obstructs the attainment of the four aims of life. (38)
If, by chance, a capable man obtains the knowledge of the victim from a Kaula,
he should first seek the Kaulika [initiation] and then again seize that mantra.
Then knowledge becomes gracious, yielding fruit and bringing about birth as it truly is; otherwise, the Goddess remains averse—how then can there be a good state for him? (40)
Furthermore, whether he be a divine being (divya) or a hero (vīra), if he is possessed of the aforementioned defects,
the disciple must not entertain the feeling of him being a guru.
However, one should abandon the desire for personal benefit and the notion of [the guru's] being a mere teacher;
whether it be a divine being or a supreme hero, there is no fault here by the command of Śiva. (42)
The Goddess said:
O God, Supreme Lord, tell me what is the distinction between one who is divine, one who is a hero, and one who is a beast; my mind is eager to hear this. (43)
The illustrious Śiva said:
Listen, O Goddess, who are adored by the world, to that supreme reality which you have asked about—
one who is divine, captivating to all, measured in speech, and firm in posture.
Profound, speaking with coherence, possessing a hundredfold attentiveness, and happy;
fearful of the lotus-feet of the Guru, yet entirely free from fear elsewhere. (45)
All-seeing, all-speaking, the warder-off of all the wicked, endowed with all virtues and divine—I am that; what is the use of many words? (46)
Fearless, a giver of fearlessness, heroic, and devoted to his guru;
eloquent, powerful, pure, and always delighting in the five elements (pañcatattva). || 47 ||
O Goddess, he possesses great enthusiasm, great intelligence, and great courage; he is magnanimous and always devoted to protecting the virtuous. (48)
O beloved, the hero Rudra himself is always composed of darkness (tamas), yet he is intensely eager for discipline;
thus, O dear one, the hero is endowed with many such qualities.
Listen, O Great Goddess, to [the description of] those who are like beasts, excluded from all the gods—those who are base, evil-minded, and revilers of the five principles (pañcatattva). (50)
O Goddess, some here are like goats, some are like rams;
some are fallen like donkeys, and others are like pigs. (51)
O Goddess, such individuals as these are to be known as beasts—wicked and the lowest of men.
For them, how could there be worship of the Goddess, spiritual accomplishment, or even initiation? (52)
Therefore, O auspicious lady, animals—which are excluded from this and cast outside the ultimate truth—are to be cut, pierced, and eaten by the heroes in every way. (53)
The Śrīdevī said:
"O Lord, something has been told, and my doubt has been stirred;
for you yourself have always described the state of the bound soul as indeed base. (54)
"Tell me, is this offering, which has been worshipped with the nature of a sacrificial animal, superior or common?
A deity does not know at all; therefore, it is certainly not offered. (55)
O Lord, ocean of compassion, quickly shatter my doubt, just as the sun dispels the darkness in an instant. (56)
Śrī Śiva said:
O wise one, you have spoken well; now listen to the refined truth. For who indeed is the protector in the Kali age of that which is called the state of a bound soul (paśubhāva)?
He does not accept the five tattvas, nor does he utter censure regarding them;
rather, he contemplates that whatever has been spoken by Śiva is the truth. (58)
He who perceives censure as a sin is proclaimed a beast;
I shall now describe his conduct, which destroys all doubt—listen! (59)
One should always eat sacrificial food (haviṣya) and should not even touch betel leaf;
nor should one touch a woman with lustful intent, except when she has bathed after her menses.
Upon seeing another's wife out of lustful intent, one should abandon gold; and like a beast, one should always renounce fish and meat. (61)
He should not partake of perfumes, garlands, fine garments, or rags;
he should always remain in the temple and go home only for the sake of food. (62)

One should always act with affection toward one's daughters, sons, and others, even if one is completely overwhelmed; one should never desire worldly power, yet if it exists, one should not abandon it. (63)
One should always practice giving if wealth is available;
thereafter, one should cast away all forms of miserliness as well as pride and other such afflictions.
O Great Goddess, one should especially avoid anger;
O Supreme Goddess, a person bound by worldly fetters (pāśava) should never perform initiation at all.
Truth, truth, and again truth—my word shall not be otherwise:
if one imparts a mantra out of ignorance or out of greed, [he incurs sin]. (66)
"Truly, truly, O Great Goddess, the curse of a goddess arises," and so forth;
we shall speak at length elsewhere of such various practices as are held by the Paśu. (67)
Nevertheless, there would be neither liberation nor any accomplishment whatsoever, even if a man were always capable of walking upon the edge of a sword. (68)
One should always practice the conduct of cattle, yet perfection is not attained;
for in Jambūdvīpa, O Goddess, a Brāhmaṇa is indeed always impure. (69)
By the command of Śiva, let there be no animal, let there be no animal, let there be no animal;
let one proceed toward the truth with the four aims of life, using milk, ghee, honey, and flour-offerings.
In the Tretā age, the Goddess was worshipped with ghee by all castes;
and in the Dvāpara age, she was worshipped with honey by all social classes.
In the Kali age, the Goddess is to be worshipped solely with intoxicating liquors and corpses;
there is no secondary alternative in Kali, O Durgā, there is no secondary alternative in the Kali age. (72)
There is no alternative rule for Brahmins [derived from] Śūdras and others in the Kali age;
there is no doubt, no doubt, no doubt regarding this in the Kali age. (73)
This is true, this is true, this which has been spoken by Śiva is true:
having taken refuge in a true guru, a person should practice the Kula conduct. (74)
"O auspicious one, does he attain divinity or does he attain heroism?
For even a divine being can accomplish on earth, without effort, that which is otherwise unattainable. (75)
O Goddess, the hero attains that state through the afflictions (kleśa) in this very life and not otherwise;
the bound soul (paśu), even in hundreds of aeons, is not capable of accomplishing it.
Just as a cripple can never leap over a mountain, so too this most secret mystery has been declared to you, O beautiful one;
it must be guarded, guarded, and always guarded, O sinless one. (77)
Thus ends the fourth chapter in the Śrī Kāmākhyā Tantra, in the dialogue between the Goddess and the Lord. || 4 ||
Now begins the fifth chapter.
The Śrīdevī said:
"Of which goddess is there this great and absolute censure by practitioners?"
O Supreme Lord, one should not perform worship without the five principles (pañcatattva).
Śrī Śiva said: O Supreme Goddess, in the Kali age, there will be the censure of all Śākta Brāhmaṇas, especially those who are devoid of the five elements (pañcatattva).
In their midst are Kālikā and Tārā, O Mistress of the Family of practitioners;
without the central [deity], their practice leads only to great laughter.
O Goddess, just as a practice without initiation is indeed a mere mockery,
so too should it always be understood for practitioners who lack the reality (tattva) of these two.
Just as no sprout can arise from seeds sown upon a stone, nor indeed can there be plowing on the earth in the absence of rain, O Goddess; || 5 ||
O Goddess, how can offspring be produced from a woman outside of her fertile season?
Just as one cannot reach a village anywhere without traveling there.
Therefore, in the sādhanas of the Goddess, one should always obtain the five principles (pañcatattva);
with these five principles, the lord of practitioners should worship joyfully according to the prescribed rule.
With liquors, meats, as well as fish, with ritual hand-gestures (mudrās), and even through sexual union—
with women— the practitioner should always worship the Mother of the World.
Otherwise, great censure is voiced by the wise and the gods;
therefore, one should be devoted to reality in body, mind, and speech. (9)
In the Kali age, that man who, having received initiation from Kālikātāriṇī, does not perform the tasting of wine, becomes fallen.
One who recites the Vedic or Tantric *saṃdhyā* prayers while excluded from the fire-sacrifice (*homa*) is declared to be a non-Brāhmaṇa; he alone is called an "elephant-like fool. (11)
Even for his ancestors, his libation is like that of one who offers urine from a swollen bladder;
therefore, he too should not offer libations if he desires his own welfare.
Having obtained the mantra of Kālītārā, he does not perform heroic conduct (vīrācāra);
therefore, the state of a Śūdra has entered his body, and not otherwise. (13)
Likewise, O Goddess, a Kṣatriya or a Vaiśya may fall into the state of a Cāṇḍāla;
indeed, a Śūdra goes to the state of a pig—of this there is no doubt. (14)
A Brāhmaṇa, a king, a Vaiśya, and a Śūdra must certainly always worship the Goddess with the five elements; they should never entertain any doubt in this matter. 15.
O Goddess, in the Kali age, for one who worships Kuleśvarī with the five principles (pañcatattva), there is nothing whatsoever in the three worlds that remains unattainable. 16.
That brāhmaṇa is indeed a Vaiṣṇava, a Śākta, and also a Gāṇapatya;
he is a Saura, a seeker of the supreme truth, and he alone is fully initiated.
He alone is righteous, virtuous, wise, and of great accomplishment;
he is a performer of sacrifices, worthy of all rites, for he is indeed a god and not otherwise.
It is universally agreed that sacred fords (tīrthas) here are purifiers for all;
yet, O Girijā, the Kaula is the purifier of even those sacred fords—what more need be said? (19)
Blessed indeed is his mother; blessed are his father and the others;
blessed are his birth, family, and kinsmen; and blessed are those people who converse with him. (20)
All the ancestors dance and joyfully sing this verse:
"Will there be someone in our lineage who will possess knowledge of the family? (21)
"Then we shall be worthy to assemble upon the floor of the assembly hall of the noble-born"—knowing this, our other ancestors became intensely eager. (22)
O Supreme Goddess, what can we say regarding the greatness of family tradition? O Queen of Devas, [tell us] also of the fruits of the eternal [practice], O Five-faced One. (23)
The Śrīdevī said:
O Lord of the Kaulas, tell me the practice that brings happiness to practitioners—divine, delightful, heart-stealing, and the bestower of all desired fruits. (24)
Śrī Śiva said:
Listen, O beloved of Kāmakalā, to the practice that brings happiness;
whatever was previously mentioned in brief, I shall now describe to you in detail.

Having beheld with devotion that most beautiful and divine place visible to the heart, and having brought forth— with a mind focused solely on the contemplation of the Supreme Goddess— the fragrance of sweet flowers that pervades it;
Indeed, one who knows the family and seeks the goal of accomplishment should stand above that. || 26 ||
O Victorious One, he who strives here should cast the flower of sound into this fortress; for by casting it there,
having abandoned the lotus-flower of long-standing worldly existence and having worshipped [the deity], he shall indeed [attain success].
If one who knows the ritual procedure recites [this], then at that very moment both he and I [shall be present]. || 27 ||
In a pure and delightful dwelling surrounded by groves, one who has smeared a large linga fashioned according to the rules with fragrant substances,
and having incensed it with various flowers and incense, [should offer] the creeper...
Now he mutters [the mantra] with great devotion; thus shall your son be born.
Having quickly suspended [the image] amidst the peak of Mount Acala and offered the "flower of sound" together with golden flowers,
and having performed manifold types of worship, one should meditate upon one's own Guru.
If even a playful person mutters [this], he is indeed Viṣṇu himself. || 29 ||
He serves with devotion; he is a group of perfected ones who remain cautious regarding the creeper-like limbs of others' wives; he enjoys the lotus-faces of others' consorts;
thus, though ageless and immortal, he triumphs in the midst of the world.
He is the sovereign of men who always follows after him. || 30 ||
Even the Lord of Lords [could not fathom] that place, which possesses fresh, pure water, is strewn with red lotuses,
is delightful with various kinds of lilies, is filled with darting fish,
and is occupied by other created beings.
O Goddess, having reached a secluded spot where the crowds of people have departed. || 31 ||
Having meditated with great devotion upon the Supreme Goddess in the heart— which is beautiful due to dense clouds and delightful with the flash of lightning—
and having completed the rites of bathing and worship according to the prescribed injunctions;
In the deep of the night, he murmurs: "What might Brahman be? || 32 ||
And here, O Mistress of the Kula, when one who knows the Kula, having received the command of the supreme Guru and placed it upon his head, worships you with a distinction of inner feeling,
who else here could he be? He is some [great being]— the Preceptor of the Gods, the Moon, or the Sun.
And someone else attains the status of a guardian of the quarters in the midst of the world. || 33 ||
Thus, if a fortunate person, even one faltering due to latent tendencies, recites this *sādhana* of the Supreme Goddess that I have spoken,
he shall attain the accomplishment of his desired fruits and become preeminent among all people.
He remains in the midst of the world, even though joined by sons and wife.
An immovable mass of wealth shall dwell in his enjoyment,
while the daily worship of the deity shall take place in his house;
and the power of his retinue shall always remain there.
He who dwells in the king's assembly with respect is also worthy of veneration. || 35 ||
Thus ends the fifth chapter in the Śrī Kāmākhyā Tantra, in the dialogue between Pārvatī and Īśvara. || 5 ||
Now begins the sixth chapter.
The Goddess said:
"O Lord of Gods, O Maheśvara, I have heard the secret concerning Kāmākhyā."
O Lord, tell me what is the means for the destruction of the great enemy? || 1 ||
Śrī Śiva said:
O Goddess, out of affection for you, I shall unfold this most profound secret.
A great-souled and steadfast master of practitioners should perform the ritual application.
Having worshipped the Great Goddess, one should accomplish [the practice] through the five principles;
having become filled with great bliss, one should perform the great sādhana.
Having taken one's own urine, one should purify it with the *kūrca* mantra;
one should then offer libations to the terrible Bhairavī or drink it oneself entirely.
One should cast [the substance] into the ten directions, into the great seats (mahāpīṭha), and even into one's own mouth;
having become naked, one should take delight therein, and the destruction of enemies will certainly occur.
If a hero should feel disgust toward semen, blood, and urine, Bhairavī will be angry with him; I tell you this as the truth, the absolute truth. (6)
O Great Goddess, whatever man, having seen or heard [this], utters censure,
he goes suddenly to hell for as long as the moon and sun endure.
O Maheśānī, one should not revile the conduct of a Vīra even in one's mind;
for he who is a Vīra, O Mahādevī, acts according to his own will and is always pure.
O Śivā, having taken an earthen vessel, one should write the name of the person to be accomplished;
then, having filled it with air, one should pour one's own urine into it.
O Maheśānī, one should recite the seed-syllable of Māyā one hundred and eight times;
O Goddess, if this is shown to Bhairavī, it will result in killing and eradication.
O Śaṅkarī, having taken his own urine with his left hand and purified it,
the best of practitioners should pour it over the body of Bhairavī.
O Maheśvarī, the enemy becomes insane or dies;
he certainly becomes deluded, agitated, or even brought under one's control.
By the mere accomplishment of the urine-rite, the heroic practitioner shall destroy an enemy equal to the thousand-eyed Indra; there is no need for deliberation on this point. (13)
The Goddess said:
"O Lord, how are semen, blood, and urine pure in this world?
Śrī Śiva said:
Listen, O Goddess, to this secret; I shall declare to you the great knowledge:
I am the semen and you are indeed the blood; from these two alone, the entire universe arises.
The entire body is indeed pure, yet it is born from semen and blood;
thus, whatever substance is produced within this elemental body, [is likewise pure]. (15)
But how, O Goddess, could a base person ever revile that which is impure?
Indeed, O Goddess, I have declared this knowledge of Brahman to you. 16.
Therefore, the entire world is pure; what need is there to mention its presence within one's own body?
O Goddess, without the knowledge of Brahman, liberation does not arise.
O Pārvatī, a knower of Brahman is Śiva himself, as well as Viṣṇu and Brahmā.
A Brāhmaṇa who is initiated, pure, and has mastered the Vedas is Śiva embodied;
it is certain that all sacred fords dwell here within his lap.
Thus ends the sixth chapter in the Śrī Kāmākhyā Tantra, in the dialogue with Pārvatī. || 6 ||
Now begins the seventh chapter.
The Goddess said:
"O Mahādeva, friend of the world, O Lord, ocean of compassion!"
Tell me of the full consecration (pūrṇābhiṣeka) for the Kaulas, which bestows both happiness and liberation.
Śrī Śiva said:
Listen, O Goddess, beloved of the Great Prāṇa, to this most wonderful [account] of the full consecration (pūrṇābhiṣeka), which fulfills all hopes and bestows the state of Śiva. 2.
Having arrived, the perfected true guru, an expert in mantra and tantra,
a follower of the Kaula path renowned among all people, shall perform the rite of consecration.
Having diligently brought together courtesans and the [sacred] principles into a pure, beautiful, and well-concealed abode approved by the Kaulikas, || 4 ||
One should respectfully settle distinguished Kaulikas right there;
one should honor the Guru with garments, ornaments, and other gifts for the sake of initiation.
One should prostrate according to the rules with devotion, satisfy [the deity] with words of praise, and with a pure heart, request: "Please declare the family dharma."
O Lord, O Śrī Guru, O ocean of compassion, make me one who has accomplished his purpose;
consecrate this practitioner who has come for refuge for the sake of service. (7)
Then, having performed the consecration, the wise one should joyfully purify the principles (tattvas),
O Dear One, after placing the jar before him with mantras, mudrās, and other rites.
Having made the ground fragrant with canopies of incense and lamps,
one should worship with various flowers, perfumes, and all necessary ritual implements.
Having completed the great worship and offered the essential elements (tattvas),
one should first offer a small portion of the grace (prasāda) to the women, and thereafter partake of it oneself.
Having fashioned the auspicious wheel according to the procedure taught in the Āgamas,
the consecrator should cause the practitioners to drink [the nectar] and should drink it himself.
They should enjoy fish, meat, and other foods, both solid and liquid; they should take delight in supreme pleasures and with courtesans according to their desire.
They should say: "May the success of the performer of the rite be firm;
may the rite of consecration quickly be accomplished without obstacle"—this is certain. (13)
O Śaṅkarī, not even a single person should emerge from the abode of the Cakra;
the practitioner should perform his morning rites and other duties right there.
Having occupied those three days, one should worship them with devotion;
then the disciple, having been consecrated, shall remain for a day and night at the beginning.
I shall describe the procedure for the performance; listen with respect, O Pārvatī.
One should procure a jar that is neither too large nor too small, which serves as the standard measure.
Whether fashioned from copper or fashioned from gold, as well as coral, diamond, pearl, and likewise gold and silver; || 17 ||
One should bring various ornaments and garments, abundant quantities of diverse articles, as well as musk, saffron, and various other perfumes. (18)
Various flowers, garlands, and the five elements (pañcatattva) prepared with effort, as well as incense and lamps made with ghee, O Supreme Goddess. (19)
Then, O Dear One, having brought the disciple to a pure abode,
the Guru should perform the worship together with courtesans and practitioners.
One should worship with devotion according to the procedure described in the chapter;
having completed the worship, one should joyfully prostrate before the Goddess with hymns of praise.
Then, O Mistress of the Kula, one should cause perfumes and garlands to be offered to Śiva and Śakti, as well as a seat, garments, and ornaments, for each of them individually.
Then, with the sounding of conchs and other instruments, and with supreme auspicious rites, one should perform the installation of the jar; listen to the procedure for that, O beloved. (23)
Having sprinkled [the vessel] with the seed-syllable of desire (Kāma-bīja), one should purify it with the Vāgbhava syllable;
having placed the jar upon Śakti, one should fill it with water by means of Māyā.
One should carefully place the five jewels, beginning with coral, therein;
and the preceptor should invoke the sacred waters (tīrthas) with this mantra: || 25 ||
Oṃ! All rivers beginning with the Gaṅgā, the oceans and the lakes;
all the seas, the streams, the ponds, the clouds, and the rivers. (26)
May the sacred lakes, the holy springs, and all the meritorious pilgrimage sites located in heaven, the netherworld, and on earth, establish their presence within this jar. (27)
One should offer the sprout with the *ramā* seed-syllable recited;
the offering of fruit should be performed with the *kūrca* mantra, and the offering of perfume and cloth with the *hṛdaya* mantra.
One should offer vermilion and flowers through the *lalanā* channel according to one's desire;
then, one should offer *dūrvā* grass with the root mantra and perform the ritual sprinkling (*abhyukṣaṇa*) with the *praṇavas*.
One should perform the striking with *darbha* grass using the mantra "huṃ phaṭ svāhā";
having meditated upon the root-pedestal, one should join it there and worship it.
The wise should make this request according to the procedure taught in the *Svatantra-tantra*.
Then, placing his hand upon that jar and gazing at the disciple, the Guru— || 31 ||
Arise, O Brahma-pitcher, bestower of the desires of the deities!
Filled with the waters of all sacred fords, fulfill this person's heart's desire. (32)
Then, O Pārvatī, the Guru should consecrate the disciple with mantras,
accompanied by all auspicious substances, along with the practitioners and the Śaktis.
O Supreme Goddess, you who bring benefit to your devotees, you cause even your disciple—who bows with sprouts such as mango leaves—to experience supreme bliss. 34.

For this consecration mantra (*abhiṣeka-mantra*), Dakṣiṇāmūrti is the seer (*ṛṣi*), Anuṣṭubh is the meter (*chandas*), Śakti is the deity (*devatā*), and its application (*viniyoga*) is for the fulfillment of all intentions of [the disciple named] so-and-so.
Oṃ! The power of the Queen of Queens, Bhairavī, Kālabhairavī.
The goddess Śmaśānabhairavī and Tripurānandabhairavī. || 35 ||
Trikuṭā, the goddess Tripurā, as well as Tripurasundarī; the great goddess Tripureśī, and likewise Tripuramālikā. || 36 ||
May the goddess Tripurānandinī and likewise Tripurātanī consecrate you with water purified by mantras. (37)
The great goddess Chinnamastā, likewise Ekajaṭeśvarī, Tārā, Jayadurgā, Śūlinī, and Bhuvaneśvarī. (38)
The Great Goddess named Tvaritā, likewise Trikhaṇḍikā, Nityā, Nityarūpā, and Vajraprastāriṇī; || 39 ||
May these, O Great Goddess—Aśvārūḍhā and likewise Mahiṣamardinī—consecrate you with water purified by mantras. (40)
Durgā, Navadurgā, Śrīdurgā, Bhagamālinī, as well as the goddess Bhagandarī, and likewise the supreme Bhagaklinnā. (41)
The goddess who is the sovereign of all wheels, likewise Nīlasarasvatī;
the goddess who bestows all accomplishments, served by Siddhas and Gandharvas. 42.
May Ugratārā, the Great Goddess, and likewise Bhadrakālī—may these [deities] consecrate you with water purified by mantra. (43)
Kṣemaṅkarī, Mahāmāyā, Aniruddhasarasvatī, Mātaṅginī, Annapūrṇā, and likewise Rājarājeśvarī. || 44 ||
May these goddesses consecrate you with water purified by mantras:
Ugracaṇḍā, Pracaṇḍā, Caṇḍogrā, and Caṇḍanāyikā. (45)
Caṇḍā, Caṇḍavatī, Caṇḍarūpā, and Aticaṇḍikā—may these sprinkle you with water purified by mantra. (46)
Ugradaṃṣṭrā, Mahādaṃṣṭrā, Śubhadaṃṣṭrā, Kapālinī, Bhīmanetrā, Viśālākṣī, Maṅgalā, Vijayā, and Jayā. || 47 ||
May these—Maṅgalā, Nandinī, Bhadrā, Lakṣmī, Kīrti, and Yaśasvinī—consecrate you with water purified by mantras. (48)
Puṣṭi, Medhā, Śivā, Sādhvī, Yaśā, Śobhā, Jayā, Dhṛti, Śrīnandā, Sunandā, Nandinī, and Nandapūjitā. (49)
May these—Vijayā, Maṅgalā, Bhadrā, Dhṛti, Śānti, Śivā, and Kṣamā—consecrate you with water purified by mantras. (50)
Siddhi, Tuṣṭi, Umā, Puṣṭi, Śrī, Ṛddhi, and likewise Rati;
Dīptā, Kānti, Yaśas, Lakṣmī, Īśvarī, and Buddhi as well. (51)
Cakrī, Jayāvatī, Brāhmī, Jayantī, Aparājitā, Ajitā, Mānavī, Śvetā, Diti, and Aditi. || 52 ||
Māyā, Mahāmāyā, Mohinī, and likewise Kṣobhiṇī;
Kamalā, Vimalā, Gaurī, and Śaraṇyambudhisundarī. (53)
Durgā, Kriyā, Arundhatī, Ghaṇṭākarṇā, Kapālinī, Raudrī, Kālī, Māyūrī, Trinetrā, and Aparājitā. || 54 ||
Surūpā, Bahurūpā, and likewise Vigrahātmikā; Carcikā is to be known as another, likewise worshipped by the gods. (55)
The Vaivasvatī, the Kaumārī, and likewise the supreme Māheśvarī;
the Vaiṣṇavī, Mahālakṣmī, Kārtikī, and likewise the Kauṣikī. || 56 ||
May Śivadūtī, Cāmuṇḍā, and she who is adorned with a garland of skulls consecrate you with water purified by mantras. (57)
Indra, Agni, Yama, Nirṛti, Varuṇa, Pavana, Kubera, Īśāna, Brahmā, and Ananta are the lords of the directions. || 58 ||
May these—year, the two solstices, months, fortnights, and days—consecrate you with water purified by mantras. (59)
May the lunar days (tithis) also consecrate you with water purified by mantras!
May the Sun, the Moon, Mars, Mercury, Jupiter, Venus, Saturn, Rāhu, and Ketu—may these planets constantly consecrate you. (60)
The lunar mansion, the karaṇa, the yoga, the nectar, and thereafter the accomplishment; likewise the burnt, the evil, the auspicious, the yogas, the days of the week, and the moments. || 61 ||
May Vāravelā, Kālavelā, Daṇḍarāśi, and the others likewise constantly consecrate [me] with water purified by mantras. 62.
Asitāṅga, Ruru, Caṇḍa, Krodha, the one known as Unmatta, Kapālī, the one named Bhīṣaṇa, and Saṃhāra— these are the eight Bhairavas.
May the sons of the Ḍākinīs and likewise the sons of the Rākiṇīs constantly consecrate [him] with water purified by mantras. (64)
Others are the sons of Lākinī, and still others are the sons of Kākinī;
furthermore, there are the sons of Śākinī and likewise the sons of Hākinī.
Then there are the sons of Dakṣiṇī and the sons of Devī;
beyond them are the sons of the Mothers, as well as the upward-facing sons.
May all those sons who face downward and those other sons who face upward consecrate you with water purified by mantras.
May Brahmā, Viṣṇu, Rudra, Īśvara, and Sadāśiva consecrate you with water purified by mantras.
The Puruṣa, Prakṛti, and the sixteen transformations are proclaimed as the Self (Ātman), the Inner Self (Antarātman), and the Supreme Knowledge-Self (Paramajñānātman). || 69 ||
May your own qualities—both those that are gross and those that are subtle—consecrate you with water purified by mantras. (70)

The seed-syllable of the Vedas and others, the *huṃ*-seed, the seed of women, the one whose banner is the fish, the seed of power (*śakti*), the seed of *Ramā*, the seed of *Māyā*, and the moon of nectar. (71)
The Cintāmaṇi, the great seed-mantra of Nārasiṃha, that of Śaṅkara, Mārtaṇḍabhairava, the seed-mantra of Durgā, and that of the illustrious Puruṣottama. (72)
May the Gāṇapatya, the Vārāha, and the Kālībīja mantras, which dispel fear,
consecrate these with water purified by mantra.
The Gaṅgā, Godāvarī, Revā, Yamunā, and Sarvasvatī; likewise the Ātreyī, Bhāratī, Sarayū, and Gaṇḍakī. || 74 ||
The Karatoyā, Candrabhāgā, Śvetagaṅgā, Kauśikī, Bhogavatī in Pātāla, and likewise the Mandākinī in heaven; || 75 ||
Let these [deities] consecrate you with water purified by mantras:
Bhairava, Bhīmarūpa, Śoṇa, and Gharghara. (76)
May Sindhu, Hṛda, and likewise those originating from Pātāla, consecrate you with water purified by mantras. || 77 ||
May all the sacred fords and holy shrines consecrate you with water purified by mantras. (78)
And may Mati, the beloved of Agni, as well as Vaṣaṭ, Kūrca, Vauṣaṭ, and Phaṭ, always consecrate me. (79)
The continents, such as Jambudvīpa and others; the oceans, such as the salt ocean and others; likewise the infinite nāgas, and the serpents such as Takṣaka and others. || 80 ||
"May these [deities] consecrate you with water purified by mantras;
may the preta-kūṣmāṇḍas, rākṣasas, and dānavas be destroyed! (81)
Piśācas, guhyakas, and bhūtas are struck down by this consecration;
so too are misfortune, Kālakarṇī, and great sins.
May diseases, sorrows, poverty, weakness, and mental disturbances perish, struck by the sprinkling of the seed-syllable of Tārā. (83)
May [all obstacles] perish when struck by the seed-syllable of Speech (Vāgbīja) during the consecration;
likewise, may there be a loss of splendor, a loss of strength, and a loss of intelligence. 84.
May poisons, untimely death, diseases, and likewise the fear of ḍākinīs and other malevolent beings, perish when struck by the empowerment of the seed-syllable of Śakti. 85.
May the terrible sorceries, the cruel planets, and likewise other serpents,
perish through this consecration, struck down by the seed-syllable of Kālī.
May all calamities perish; may all prosperities remain steadfast;
and may all desires be fulfilled through this empowerment of Śakti. (87)
Then the Guru should indeed initiate again one who has already received the mantra;
then success will truly come to pass—this is my word, not otherwise. 88.
Then, with great joy, one should prostrate many times before the Goddess and the Guru;
one should give a sacrificial fee to the Guru consisting of gold and refined gold according to one's means. (89)
One should satisfy [the deity] with various garments, ornaments, perfumes, garlands, and the like, as well as with words of praise, and indeed bow down once again. (90)
With body, mind, and speech, the Guru should bestow such blessings;
through various acts of affection, he should cause the disciple to grasp the supreme reality.
And the Guru should sport joyfully together with the Bhairavas and their Śaktis;
the Bhairavas and the Śaktis, for their part, should bestow blessings with great effort. (92)
Likewise, the wise one should feed the Bhairavas for three days;
on the eighth day, he should again perform the sprinkling (secana) upon the disciple.
O Goddess, the wise man, reciting the Vidyā of kings with water from copper vessels,
as well as the *kundukas*, does so, O Beloved, for the sake of the sevenfold prosperity.
Then, O Goddess, the practitioner should diligently offer garments and ornaments to the Śaktis and the Bhairavas; know this to be the conclusion.
The Śrī Devī said:
"O Lord of Gods, I have heard the secret concerning the rite of consecration; tell me that, O Lord, as to how one becomes a Guru authorized in the Kaula tradition. (96)
Śrī Śiva said:
A great knower, a lord of the Kaulas, pure and devoted to the Guru, capable of both restraint and grace, and intent upon protecting his disciples. (97)
But a virtuous person who is endowed with sons, wife, and other kin, who is honored, and who possesses constant faith in the Āgama—he alone is qualified for this office, and no one else. (98)
O Giver of Boons, a wise person should always avoid one who is blind, lame, diseased, possessed of only meager knowledge, or merely an ordinary Kaula. (99)
One who desires success should especially avoid an indifferent person;
for initiation from the mouth of an indifferent person is as fruitless, O Dear One, as a barren woman. 100.
O Goddess, if a base person, out of ignorance or delusion, should consecrate one who is indifferent [to his duty], obstacles shall beset him at every step.
What is the use of his recitations and worship? What is the use of meditations or devotion? For all of that is indeed fruitless for him, and in the end he goes to hell. (102)
O Goddess, he shall dwell perpetually in hell for hundreds of millions of kalpas;
only after many such births shall he obtain the mantra of the Goddess.
Then, having approached the pure householder preceptor who has been appointed for that purpose, he should again perform the rites of consecration with great effort. (104)
Indeed, all his actions will always certainly bear fruit;
even knowledge is equal to a mother, O beloved, for it constantly protects him from what has fallen [into misfortune]. 105.
Just as one should abandon a sacrificial animal and instead worship a Kaula Guru,
so too should one abandon a hundred consecrations performed by an indifferent person.
Śiva himself is truly consecrated when one is initiated;
he alone is the blessed Brāhmaṇa who is devoted solely to the Goddess and the God. || 107 ||
O Pārvatī, listen: only his birth on this earth is fruitful;
only his actions are fruitful; and only his wealth is fruitful. (108)
For him alone is Dharma fruitful, and for him desire is fruitful;
O Goddess, his initiation is indeed fruitful, his ritual action is fruitful, and his body is fruitful.
O Girijā, everything of his indeed bears fruit; what need is there for further words?
In whatever place a holy man may dwell, that place is equal to Vārāṇasī.
All sacred fords (tīrthas) certainly dwell here within his lap;
this is the truth, the truth, O Mahāmāyā, and again the truth that I have spoken.
O Pārvatī, whatever secret initiations have been described here in all the tantras, they do not equal even a sixteenth part of this one.
O Goddess of the gods, this chapter does not come into being without a worthy guru and a worthy disciple; I have spoken the truth, the absolute truth. (113)
But this sprinkling, O Goddess, is difficult to obtain in the three worlds;
here, O Pārvatī, Gaṇeśa and Kārttikeya are themselves the vessels.
O Supreme Goddess, one who is equal to me, equal to Brahmā, or equal to Viṣṇu is a fit vessel here;
even with five mouths, O Parameśvarī, he cannot be fully described.
Thus has been told to you this secret, supreme, and great sprinkling (secana). It must be concealed, concealed, concealed with great effort. || 116 ||
Just as pleasure is to be concealed, so too is the supreme consecration;
just as a man, having found buried wealth, would guard it with care.
In that very same way, O Mahāmāyā, it must be kept secret at my command. || 117 ||
Thus ends the seventh chapter in the Śrī Kāmākhyā Tantra, in the dialogue between Pārvatī and Īśvara. || 7 ||
Now begins the eighth chapter.
The Śrī Devī said:
"O Mahādeva, O ocean of compassion, tell me the true nature of liberation."
In which [work] the six philosophical systems here have been rendered objects of ridicule. || 1 ||
Śrī Śiva said:
Listen, O auspicious and wise Goddess, to that supreme reality which you have asked about.
O Queen of the Gods, I know this secret, as does Hari.
Just as the world deceives children with sweetmeats, O Goddess, so does a king bind the wicked man with a staff. || 3 ||
O fair-faced one, if liberation were possible for a wicked person, then even a barbarian who is not accepted by the world and its philosophical systems would be considered worthy of hope.
O Dear One, like animals fallen into the great well of the six philosophical systems,
they do not know the ultimate reality, just as a ladle does not know the taste of the soup it stirs.
There is no core in the plantain tree, nor in the castor-oil plant, O fair-faced one;
likewise, O Goddess, there is no liberation in the philosophical systems—this has been declared by me.
Just as deer turn away from a mirage,
so too do those seeking liberation turn away from [false] perceptions.
And by the grace of the glorious Guru, one shall always first attain liberation;
thereafter, the wise person may wander through all the scriptures out of curiosity.
I shall proclaim the true nature of liberation; listen with reverence, O Pārvatī, to that by which one assumes a body here again and again.
First there is the favor of the Goddess, and immediately after that, from the mouth of the illustrious Guru;
from that, long-lasting devotion toward her is born.
For from that, the means of accomplishment is pure; from that, knowledge is perfectly stainless.
From knowledge, liberation arises—this is the definitive conclusion of the scripture. (11)
Liberation is said to be fourfold, O fair-faced one: sālokya, sārūpya, sāmīpya, and indeed nirvāṇa, which is higher than the highest. (12)
Sālokya is residence in the same world; sārūpya is having the same form;
sāyujya is being joined with a portion [of the deity]; and nirvāṇa is the dissolution of the mind. || 13 ||
The Goddess said:
"That which is called the perfect dissolution of a person, namely Nirvāṇa—tell me what that is, O Mahādeva; resolve my doubt regarding this dissolution. (14)
Śrī Śiva said:
O ocean of compassion, liberation for the asuras consists of their manifestation and dissolution; having eliminated them because of their wickedness, I sport with the gods. (15)
O Śaṅkarī, know that liberation consists of the dissolution of the mind;
it has been attained by me, by Viṣṇu, by Brahmā, and by Nārada and others.

That which is *sālokya* (dwelling in the same realm) alone, as well as that which is joined with *sārūpya* (attaining the same form)—these two [are attained]; however, one who possesses *sāyujya* (union) attains all three, for it is indeed the complete liberation (*nirvāṇa*).
O Dear One, liberation, dark like the petal of a blue lotus and residing within two petals,
always remains full and vibrates incessantly for one who is liberated.
She is eternal, worshipped by the world, and whose nature is existence, consciousness, and bliss;
she alone is the supreme Mother, the bestower of all desired objects. (19)
In the desired [state], the connection is immovable, and that is proclaimed as Nirvāṇa;
it is the knowledge of liberation, the knowledge of the Kula, and no other knowledge, O Mistress of the Kula. (20)
O Goddess of gods, know for certain that among all virtuous people, those who become liberated in heaven, on earth, or in the netherworld, [attain this state]. || 21 ||
The liberation of all has been thus, and will be thus;
likewise, the means for bestowing liberation should be known through the five principles (pañcatattva). || 22 ||
But the grace of the Goddess, O Goddess, which reveals the path of the Kula, is initiation consisting of the Kula, received from the lotus-face of the venerable Guru. (23)
Devotion toward the substances of the Kula is considered the bestower of liberation;
having understood this, the wise man should diligently cultivate the knowledge of the Kula. (24)
O Goddess, if this mantra is obtained by the power of fortune, it is the cause of liberation; it is known by oneself and not otherwise.
O Maheśvarī, the truth of liberation, which has not been heard by others, has indeed been told to you;
O Goddess, it must be kept secret by my command, just as one's own source of birth is kept secret.
Thus ends the eighth chapter in the Śrī Kāmākhyā Tantra, in the dialogue between Pārvatī and Īśvara.
Now begins the ninth chapter.
The venerable Goddess said: "O Mahādeva, that which was described as Kāmākhyā, who possesses all forms—"
Tell me, O Lord of the World, who is she? O Master, do not practice deception.
O Lord, I would even resort to deceit if I were to swear an oath before you;
for what woman, when in love, would properly display her private parts to her husband?
Having heard these words of Girijā, Śaṅkara laughed and said: ||| 2 ||
The illustrious Śiva said:
Listen, O Goddess, you who are as dear to me as my own life; I shall tell it to you.
That Goddess Kālikā is the Mother, the embodiment of all vidyās.
She alone is renowned as Kāmākhyā; this is the truth, the absolute truth, and not otherwise.
Know that she alone is Brahman; the various philosophical systems (darśanas) exist merely for the sake of designation.
And they move about full of longing, like cakora birds toward the moon;
for from her indeed is born this entire world, both moving and unmoving. (5)
And they dissolve back into her; do not entertain doubt, O beloved.
She is the Goddess who is gross, subtle, and supreme, whose nature is existence, consciousness, and bliss.
She is considered to be of immeasurable prowess and dark-hued, an ocean of compassion;
she consists of liberation, is the sustainer of the world, and is likewise eternally composed of bliss.
The power of action is the supporter of the universe, and Tārā is indeed eternal;
just as at the completion of a rite, the sacrificial fee (dakṣiṇā) bestows the attainment of the fruit.
Likewise, O Goddess, this [form] bestows the fruit of liberation for all;
therefore, O lady of excellent complexion, she is called Dakṣiṇākālī.
Kālī is always black in color; this is the conclusion of the Āgama. All tantras have been spoken, and it is determined by this tantra. (10)
Having performed this for the fulfillment of his resolve, the wise man should cause it to be recited regarding his desires;
or, having recited it himself, he should cause it to be heard—if one hears it or worships it.
By the grace of the glorious Kālī, one attains whatever desire one may have;
O Goddess, this supreme tantra is just like the philosopher’s stone. 12.
Just as the wish-fulfilling tree is a giver, so should it be understood by the wise;
just as all jewels are certainly found in the ocean. (13)
Likewise, O fair-faced one, all perfections—both worldly enjoyment and liberation—are established here;
just as Meru is the abode of all the gods, so it is once again established.
O Goddess, I declare by oath that this tantra, endowed with all branches of knowledge and dispelling fear, shall abide in whosever home. (15)
There is never even a trace of disease, grief, or sin;
there is no fear of robbers there, nor any fear of planets or kings.
There shall be no fear of portents there, nor likewise any fear of pestilence;
indeed, O Goddess, I declare that they shall have no fear of defeat. (17)
There shall be no fear anywhere for any of the bhūtas, pretas, piśācas, dānavas, or rākṣasas, nor likewise for tigers and other such beasts. (18)
There is no fear of the Kūṣmāṇḍas, nor any fear of fire and the like; likewise, there is no fear from any of the Vināyakas or from the Gandharvas. (19)
O Goddess, whatever terrifying beings exist in heaven, on earth, or in the netherworld— whether they be predatory or creators of obstacles— they have no cause for fear.
The messengers of Yama flee with their faces turned away, overwhelmed by fear;
truly, truly, O Great Goddess, I speak this under oath. (21)
In that place, incomparable prosperity shall endure for seven generations;
likewise, by the grace of the Goddess, speech itself is said to be immovable.
This has been told to you, O Goddess; it must never be disclosed.
It is to be kept secret, kept secret, kept secret always, O Beloved.
This must be guarded with special effort, especially from the uninitiated;
one should not speak of it even in the presence of practitioners who have fallen from their path.
One should not give to those who are one-eyed or lame, nor likewise to those who are censured;
nor even should one speak [of such things] in the presence of indifferent people.
By my command, it must not be given to a hypocrite, nor especially to one who lacks devotion; nor to a fool, nor to one devoid of sincere intent, nor to a pauper. (26)
O Maheśvarī, by the command of Śiva, one should give it to a peaceful and pure Kaulika,
to a devotee of Kālī, and to a Śaiva or Vaiṣṇava.
To him who is endowed with the state of non-duality, who meditates upon Mahākāla, who honors gods, women, and ascetics, and who offers oblations to Śivā; || 28 ||
Thus ends the ninth chapter in the Śrī Kāmākhyā Tantra, in the dialogue between Pārvatī and Īśvara. 9.
And this treatise is completed.
